title: Lancaster Street and Highway 85 ramp closures
subtitle: Also: Cambridge brownfield grant, Stage 2 ION deferral, water supply strategy, roundabouts, entrepreneurial grants, e-scooters.
overview: The Planning and Works Committee recommended permanently closing both ramps at the Highway 85 and Lancaster Street interchange in Kitchener {{vote:m3}}. An alternative to keep the ramps open and signalize the Bridgeport Road off-ramp was defeated {{vote:m2}}. The recommendation goes to Regional Council. The closure would still require final approval of the environmental assessment and a request to the Ministry of Transportation.

The committee also recommended a Joint Tax Increment Grant for 130 Water Street North in Cambridge, capped at $6,801,489 for the Region {{vote:m9}}. It endorsed guiding principles for the Water Supply Strategy {{vote:m11}} and recommended full funding of $138,000 for five entrepreneurial grants {{vote:m12}}. Discussion of Stage 2 ION was deferred to the June 6, 2023 meeting {{vote:m10}}.

On the consent agenda, the committee recommended speed and pedestrian crossover by-law changes for three roundabouts {{vote:m5}}, expropriation of land for the Sawmill Road and Ebycrest Road roundabout {{vote:m6}}, and interim active transportation improvements on Myers Road {{vote:m8}}. It also received reports on a shared e-scooter and e-bike program and on greenhouse gas emissions.

decisions.item: Lancaster Street and Highway 85 ramp closure
decisions.detail: The committee recommended endorsing permanent closure of both ramps, filing the Notice of Completion, and asking the Ministry of Transportation to include their removal in a future highway project {{vote:m3}}.

decisions.item: Alternative to keep Lancaster ramps open
decisions.detail: A motion to oppose the closure, keep the ramps operating and request signals at the Bridgeport Road off-ramp was defeated {{vote:m2}}.
The committee recommended a new Joint Tax Increment Grant agreement for the Cambridge site, with the Regional amount not to exceed $6,801,489 {{vote:m9}}.
The committee deferred the related motion to its June 6, 2023 meeting {{vote:m10}}.
The committee recommended endorsing the strategy's guiding principles {{vote:m11}}.
The committee recommended fully funding all five eligible applicants for $138,000, above the $76,000 staff had proposed from the 2023 budget {{vote:m12}}.
The committee recommended authorizing the Regional Solicitor to start expropriation of partial lands at four properties for the roundabout {{vote:m6}}.
The committee recommended interim active transportation and traffic calming measures, plus two new pedestrian crossovers {{vote:m8}}.
